good.post: $LUMEN gained 7.9% on $34.2M volume, about 2.2x its $15.6M average, while BTC moved just 0.8% over the same day. The token now trades at $1.73, up from $1.60 at the open, and the volume stayed elevated after the move. The gap raises one specific question: what drove participation to 2.2x the average on a day when the wider market barely moved?
good.why: Question: one specific data question about the volume gap on a flat market day.

good.post: $ATLAS fell 6.4% to $0.88 on $19.7M volume, roughly 1.6x the $12.3M average, while the rest of the market stayed flat. Sellers showed up steadily through the session, and no bounce attempt appeared before the close. The tape leaves one question unanswered: why did volume rise while buyers stayed away, when the last three dips at this level all found support within a day?
good.why: Question: why volume rose while buyers stayed away at a level that held before.

good.post: $VERA traded $27.8M, about 3.1x its $9.0M average, yet price moved only 0.9% to $2.14. Volume at that level with price going nowhere is the anomaly here. Either buyers absorbed a large amount of supply, or sellers distributed into strength without pushing price down. Which one was it? The next session should give the answer, since volume this high rarely stays silent for long.
good.why: Question: which side was behind 3.1x volume on a flat price.
